questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which selector has the HIGHEST specificity weight among the following?
questions.explanation: ID selectors (#id) have specificity weight (1,0,0), higher than classes (0,1,0) or elements (0,0,1).

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What is the specificity calculation tuple (Inline, ID, Class, Element) for `.nav ul li.active a`?
questions.explanation: Two classes (`.nav`, `.active`) and three elements (`ul`, `li`, `a`) yield specificity (0, 0, 2, 3).

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What does the `!important` keyword do when added to a CSS declaration?

options.B: Overrides standard cascade specificity rules for that declaration
options.C: Applies property to all child elements

questions.explanation: !important overrides normal declaration cascade rules regardless of selector specificity.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: If an element has `width: 200px; padding: 20px; border: 5px solid black; box-sizing: content-box;`, what is its total rendered physical width?
questions.explanation: With content-box: Total width = width (200) + left/right padding (40) + left/right border (10) = 250px.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: If an element has `width: 200px; padding: 20px; border: 5px solid black; box-sizing: border-box;`, what is its total rendered physical width?
questions.explanation: With border-box: Total width is fixed to 200px; padding and border are absorbed inside the 200px width.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What is margin collapsing in CSS?

options.A: Margins of adjacent block elements collapse into a single margin equal to the largest margin size
options.D: Negative margins cancel out positive margins

questions.explanation: Top and bottom margins of adjacent block boxes combine into a single margin equal to max(margin1, margin2).

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which property specifies the z-order/stacking order of overlapping positioned elements?
questions.explanation: z-index sets the z-order axis position for positioned elements (position != static).

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: How does `position: sticky;` behave during scrolling?

options.A: Remains static until a scroll threshold relative to container/viewport is met, then behaves as fixed

questions.explanation: position: sticky toggles between relative and fixed depending on scroll offset relative to viewport/container bounds.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which flex property determines if flex items wrap onto multiple lines when space runs out?
questions.explanation: flex-wrap (values: nowrap, wrap, wrap-reverse) controls whether flex container wraps items.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What is the shorthand `flex: 1;` equivalent to?
questions.explanation: Single number unitless value `flex: 1;` expands to `flex-grow: 1; flex-shrink: 1; flex-basis: 0%;`.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which flex item property defines the initial size of an item before remaining space is distributed?
questions.explanation: flex-basis sets initial default sizing of a flex item before free space distribution.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which property sets grid row and column gaps simultaneously in modern CSS?
questions.explanation: The shorthand `gap` property (formerly grid-gap) sets gutters between rows and columns.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What does `grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);` create?

options.A: 3 equal-width flexible columns spanning total available grid width

questions.explanation: repeat(3, 1fr) creates three tracks each taking an equal fraction (1fr) of free space.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which property specifies explicit named areas in a grid container layout?
questions.explanation: grid-template-areas defines named grid cell layout areas using string templates.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What is the key difference between pseudo-classes (`:hover`) and pseudo-elements (`::before`) in CSS syntax?

options.A: Pseudo-classes select state/condition of existing elements; pseudo-elements style dynamic sub-parts or injected content
options.B: Pseudo-classes use double colons; pseudo-elements single

questions.explanation: Pseudo-classes (single colon) target states; pseudo-elements (double colon) style dynamic structural parts/content.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which pseudo-element requires the `content: "";` property to render inserted content before an element?
questions.explanation: ::before (and ::after) pseudo-elements require content property to generate rendering boxes.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which pseudo-class targets every element that is the N-th child of its parent?
questions.explanation: :nth-child(n) matches elements based on their numeric position index in parent children list.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What is the difference between `:nth-child(2)` and `:nth-of-type(2)`?

options.A: :nth-child(2) selects second child regardless of tag type; :nth-of-type(2) selects second child matching that specific tag type

questions.explanation: :nth-child counts all sibling elements; :nth-of-type counts only siblings matching element tag filter.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.topic: Functions such as calc(), min(), max(), and clamp()
questions.question: What does `width: calc(100% - 50px);` calculate in CSS?

options.A: Subtracts 50px from 100% parent container width dynamically at runtime

questions.explanation: calc() performs runtime mathematical calculations mixing different CSS length units.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.topic: Functions such as calc(), min(), max(), and clamp()
questions.question: How does `font-size: clamp(1rem, 2.5vw, 2rem);` restrict font sizing?

options.A: Sets font-size to preferred 2.5vw, clamped between minimum 1rem and maximum 2rem bounds

questions.explanation: clamp(MIN, VAL, MAX) clamps a value between lower and upper defined threshold limits.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which CSS attribute selector targets elements whose `href` attribute ENDS with `.pdf`?
questions.explanation: The $= attribute selector matches string endings.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which attribute selector matches elements whose `href` attribute STARTS with `https`?
questions.explanation: The ^= attribute selector matches string prefix beginnings.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which attribute selector matches elements whose attribute contains a substring anywhere inside it?
questions.explanation: The *= attribute selector matches substring occurrences anywhere within the value.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What does the direct child combinator selector `div > p` select?

options.A: Paragraphs that are immediate direct children of a div
options.B: All paragraphs inside a div regardless of nesting depth
options.C: Paragraphs placed directly after a div sibling

questions.explanation: The > combinator selects elements that are direct immediate children of the specified parent.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What does the adjacent sibling combinator `h1 + p` select?

options.A: The paragraph immediately following the h1 element at same parent level

questions.explanation: The + combinator selects the single sibling element immediately following the first element.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What does general sibling combinator `h1 ~ p` select?

options.A: All paragraph siblings following an h1 at same parent depth

questions.explanation: The ~ combinator matches all sibling elements following the initial element sharing parent.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What screen width orientation does `@media (min-width: 768px)` target?

options.A: Screens with width of 768px or wider (desktops/tablets)

questions.explanation: min-width: 768px applies styles when viewport width is greater than or equal to 768px (mobile-first).

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which transform property specifies the pivot point for element rotation or scaling?
questions.explanation: transform-origin sets the origin location for an element's transformations (default: 50% 50%).

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which @-rule is used to define keyframe steps for CSS animations?
questions.explanation: The @keyframes at-rule defines animation sequence keyframe stages.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which property makes a CSS animation repeat indefinitely?
questions.explanation: animation-iteration-count: infinite specifies non-stopping animation loop cycles.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which `animation-fill-mode` value retains styles applied by the last keyframe after animation ends?
questions.explanation: forwards retains computed values from the final keyframe after animation completion.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which property specifies how to handle content that overflows an element's box bounds horizontally and vertically?
questions.explanation: overflow (values: visible, hidden, scroll, auto) controls clipped or scrollable container overflow.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which CSS property enables smooth scrolling animations when navigating via internal anchor links?
questions.explanation: scroll-behavior: smooth enables smooth animated scrolling behavior for viewport scrolling.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which property ensures an `` fills its container box while preserving aspect ratio by clipping excess?
questions.explanation: object-fit: cover scales image to maintain aspect ratio while filling container box, clipping if necessary.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which property scales an image to fit entirely inside its container without clipping, preserving aspect ratio?
questions.explanation: object-fit: contain letterboxes/scales image so entire asset is visible without cropping.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.topic: Inheritance and the CSS box model
questions.question: Which CSS keyword explicitly forces an element to inherit a property value from its parent element?
questions.explanation: The `inherit` keyword causes element to adopt computed property value of parent.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.topic: Inheritance and the CSS box model
questions.question: Which CSS keyword resets a property to its default initial browser specification value?
questions.explanation: The `initial` keyword sets property to official CSS specification default value.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What does BEM stand for in CSS methodology naming conventions?
questions.explanation: BEM (Block Element Modifier) is a component-based class naming methodology for clean CSS.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which media query detects if user requested OS-level reduced motion/animation settings?
questions.explanation: prefers-reduced-motion detects system preferences for minimizing unnecessary non-essential animations.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: How does `display: inline-block;` differ from standard `display: inline;`?

options.A: inline-block respects width, height, top/bottom padding and margins while flowing inline with text

questions.explanation: inline-block behaves inline in document flow but allows width/height and block box dimensions.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What establishes an absolute positioning reference container for an element with `position: absolute;`?

options.A: The nearest ancestor element with position other than static

questions.explanation: position: absolute positions relative to nearest ancestor whose position is relative, absolute, fixed, or sticky.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which flex property controls individual child item alignment overriding container `align-items`?
questions.explanation: align-self allows individual flex items to override container align-items alignment.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What is the shorthand property for setting both `grid-row-start` and `grid-row-end`?
questions.explanation: grid-row (e.g., `grid-row: 1 / 3;`) sets grid item starting and ending track lines.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which property creates CSS linear gradient backgrounds?
questions.explanation: linear-gradient() function is applied as a value on background-image property.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which CSS property alters character horizontal letter spacing?
questions.explanation: letter-spacing controls tracking/space between individual text characters.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What is a Reflow (Layout phase) in browser rendering pipeline?

options.A: Browser process calculating geometry and position layout coordinates for DOM elements

questions.explanation: Reflow computes layout positions and geometry for elements when structural dimensions change.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What is Repaint in browser rendering?

options.A: Redrawing pixels on screen when visual elements change (like color) without affecting geometry layout dimensions

questions.explanation: Repaint occurs when visual appearances (e.g., color, outline) change without altering box dimensions/layout.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: How do you fix element overflow causing unexpected horizontal scrollbars on mobile viewports?

options.A: Apply `max-width: 100%;` on images/containers and check bounds

questions.explanation: Preventing fixed-pixel widths and setting max-width: 100% on media prevents viewport overflow.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What does `justify-content: space-between;` do in a flex container?

options.A: Distributes items evenly; first item at start edge, last item at end edge
options.C: Puts equal space around all items including ends

questions.explanation: space-between places equal gaps between items, locking edge items flush against container boundaries.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What does `justify-content: space-around;` do?

options.A: Distributes items evenly with equal space on both sides of every item (half-size spaces at ends)

questions.explanation: space-around surrounds items with equal padding space, producing half-size gaps at outer edges.
